How Shizuku+ works with other apps

Shizuku+ provides exclusive Plus features (Storage Bridge, AI Bridge, Theming Bridge) accessible via this app and any third-party app explicitly targeting the Shizuku+ API (af.shizuku.plus.api).

Important: Shizuku+ is fully backwards compatible with the original Shizuku API. Existing apps that use stock Shizuku (like SD Maid SE and SwiftBackup) will automatically discover and work with Shizuku+ without any developer updates required.

Using alongside stock Shizuku: Only one service can run at a time. The Companion card on the home screen makes switching easy if you still have stock Shizuku installed, but it is recommended to uninstall stock Shizuku and use Shizuku+ exclusively.

Dhizuku allows Shizuku to share its Device Owner (DevicePolicyManager) privileges with third-party apps. This is essential for apps like Dhizuku Manager or certain kiosk-mode tools that need to manage system policies without being the sole Device Owner themselves.

The Shell Accelerator intercepts standard shell commands (am, pm, settings) and translates them directly into Shizuku server API calls. This avoids the high overhead of spawning a new /system/bin/sh process for every command, making automation in MacroDroid or Tasker significantly faster and more battery-efficient.

Android Virtualization Framework (AVF) Manager allows you to run isolated Linux or Microdroid virtual machines. On supported hardware (Snapdragon 8 Gen 1+, Tensor G2+), this enables hardware-accelerated virtualization with VirtIO-GPU support for running desktop Linux environments or isolated secure tasks.

The Storage Bridge provides authenticated, high-speed access to restricted filesystem paths like /data/data/ (app data) and /data/app/ (APK files). This allows backup tools like Neo Backup to function without full root access, while maintaining security through Shizuku\'s permission model.

Continuity Bridge allows Shizuku+ devices on the same network to hand off tasks and synchronize clipboard/app state. This utilizes the Android 17 Handoff APIs (backported where possible) to allow seamless transitions of automation tasks between your phone and tablet.

The Intelligence Bridge grants AI assistants privileged access to screen content and NPU scheduling. It enables features like "Circle to Search" or screen-aware context for local LLMs by providing high-performance, window-aware frame capture that bypasses standard Android screen recording restrictions.

Window Tuner exposes advanced WindowManager flags that allow any app to be forced into free-form mode, placed in a persistent Bubble Bar, or rendered with always-on-top overlays. This is a powerful tool for multitasking and customizing the OneUI desktop experience.

This bridge provides rootless access to the OverlayManagerService (OMS). It uses modern OverlayManagerTransactions to register Fabricated Overlays, allowing apps like Hex Installer to modify system colors, fonts, and dimensions on OneUI 6/7/8 without requiring a rooted device.

The Network Governor provides privileged access to the INetworkPolicyManager and Private DNS settings. It can enforce POLICY_REJECT_ALL for individual apps, providing a robust, system-level firewall that works even on Wi-Fi and 5G connections without an active VPN tunnel.

Deep Process Control allows the server to bypass standard app-hibernation and standby restrictions. It can force apps into the RESTRICTED standby bucket or perform a true deepForceStop (killing all services and background jobs), which is essential for aggressive battery-saving tools.

Returns a fake version string for the \'busybox\' command to satisfy legacy script requirements.

Many apps check for root by looking for Magisk-specific properties or the /sbin/.magisk folder. This module simulates these elements, allowing you to use root-only features in apps that refuse to start without detecting a Magisk environment.

Legacy root apps often try to grant themselves permissions via shell. This bridge listens for these \'pm grant\' calls and uses Shizuku\'s elevated privileges to approve them instantly, avoiding manual permission management.

When apps copy files to /data/data using a standard shell, they often lose ownership and SELinux contexts. This module automatically adds flags like --preserve=all to maintain file integrity and prevent app crashes.

BusyBox is a suite of Unix utilities common on rooted devices. Some older root apps check for its existence before running their logic. This module returns a simulated successful response for the \'busybox\' command.

Control the status bar and Quick Settings panel: collapse/expand the shade, toggle expansion lock, and manage tile layout — all without user interaction.

Grants privileged access to the status bar and Quick Settings panel via the system statusbar service. Apps and automations can collapse or expand the notification shade, lock expansion to prevent user access, click individual QS tiles, and read or rewrite the full tile list — all without requiring the device to be unlocked or user gestures.
Grant or revoke runtime permissions without prompts, silently install APKs, debloat system apps per-user, and suspend/restore apps with full data preservation — all via privileged shell access.

Exposes privileged package management operations available to the ADB/shell process: runtime permission grant/revoke (pm grant/revoke), user-scoped system app uninstall (pm uninstall --user 0) and restore (pm install-existing), data-safe app suspension (pm suspend/unsuspend), and silent APK install with automatic permission grants. These are genuine root-class capabilities that work on any device running Shizuku over ADB without needing actual root access.
Override display resolution and DPI — the same as adb shell wm size/density — so apps and automation can adjust screen layout without requiring ADB access themselves.

Provides privileged display configuration via the wm shell tool: override resolution (wm size) and density (wm density) on the fly, read current and physical values, and reset overrides to device defaults. Useful for fixing app layout issues, forcing a specific aspect ratio for screen recording, desktop mode tweaks, and accessibility scaling — historically a root-only capability now available through the ADB shell process.
